newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya says defiant aircraft back to Tripoli.
newsitem.headline: Libya says defiant aircraft back to Tripoli.

text.p: Libya said on Thursday a Libyan plane which flew to Ghana in defiance of a 1992 United Nations ban on its international flights returned back to Tripoli.
The official Libyan news agency JANA, monitored in Tunis, did not say when the Libyan Arab Airlines aircraft returned nor if it landed in any other African country.
The plane had flown an official Libyan foreign ministry delegation to Ghana's capital Accra for talks with Ghanaian officials.
In Accra, Ghana's deputy foreign minister Mohamed Chamas told reporters on Thusrday that Ghana was not informed beforehand of a Libyan plane coming.
He said the Boeing 727 signalled before landing on Tuesday night in Accra that it had only about one hour and 20 minutes fuel left.
"Under those circumstances, air traffic control allowed a technical landing," he said.

Libya said it had told the Security Council that it considered itself no longer subject to the U.N. embargo after it gave permission for an American-piloted balloon to overfly its territory last week.

Libya has on several occasions violated a ban on international flights which is part of sanctions imposed by the United Nations in 1992 after it refused to hand over two Libyans indicted in the United States and Britain for their alleged role in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in which 270 people have been killed.
